properties.description:
* WHAT...Heavy, wet snow expected. Total snow accumulations between
10 and 20 inches, with the exception of the Lincoln valley where up
to 7 inches is expected. Isolated amounts approaching 30 inches
within the Bob Marshall Wilderness. Winds gusting as high as 45
mph.

* WHERE...Gates of the Mountains, Upper Blackfoot and MacDonald Pass,
Southern High Plains, and Southern Rocky Mountain Front.

* WHEN...Until 6 AM MDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Gusty winds combined with
the wet and heavy nature of the snow could bring down tree
branches. Isolated power outages are possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snowfall amounts will vary drastically from
grassy surfaces to roadways, most notably at lower elevations, with
accumulations on non-grassy surfaces being confined mainly to
between the evening through late morning hours.
properties.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, and water in your
vehicle in case of an emergency. The latest road conditions for the
state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued October 10 at 12:47PM EDT until October 10 at 2:45PM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
SMWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Apalachee Bay or Coastal Waters From Keaton Beach to Ochlockonee
River Fl out to 20 Nm...
Coastal waters from  Suwannee River to Keaton Beach out 20 NM...
Waters from Suwannee River to Apalachicola FL from 20 to 60 NM...

* Until 245 PM EDT.

* At 1247 PM EDT, severe thunderstorms capable of producing
waterspouts were located along a line extending from 10 nm
northeast of Buckeye Reef to 22 nm south of V Tower, moving
northeast at 25 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats...damage
vessels...and create suddenly higher waves. Make sure all
on board are in a secure location and wearing life
jackets. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34
knots...suddenly higher waves...frequent lightning...and
heavy downpours. Make sure all on board are wearing life
jackets.

* Locations impacted include...
Buckeye Reef.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 10 at 12:42PM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Florida...

Shoal River near Mossy Head (CR 1087) affecting Walton County.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Shoal River near Mossy Head (CR 1087).

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 22.0 feet, Water reaches the base of the New Harmony
Road bridge. Water begins to cross Williams Road near the Mill
Creek Bridge. Nearly all residences on Plantation lane are flooded
at this level.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:15 AM CDT Saturday the stage was 22.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 11:15 AM CDT Saturday was 22.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall to 14.2 feet Monday
morning.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 22.3
feet on 01/21/2010.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1000 PM CDT.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING NOW IN EFFECT UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE
